stories.title: India’s security chief Ajit Doval visits China for border talks ahead of BRICS meeting
stories.summary: India's National Security Adviser Ajit Doval is in Beijing for talks with Chinese officials on their disputed Himalayan border before the upcoming BRICS summit in September. The talks aim to maintain peace and stability along the 3,500km border, despite past clashes and territorial disputes, including over Arunachal Pradesh. The BRICS summit in New Delhi will focus on Middle East issues, trade, and global power shifts, with China expected to participate amid improving bilateral ties. New Delhi – India’s top security official arrived in Beijing on Aug 24 for talks on the countries’ disputed Himalayan border, ahead of a BRICS summit in September that New Delhi hopes Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend. India’s Ministry of External Affairs said that National Security Adviser Ajit Doval will meet Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi for talks on Aug 25. “Doval, India’s Special Representative (SR) on the India-China Boundary Question, arrived in Beijing on a two-day visit earlier this afternoon,” it said. Doval will also meet China’s Vice-President Han Zheng, it added. The two side have met repeatedly for talks about their border since a deadly 2020 clash. “At this meeting, the two sides will, in accordance with the spirit of the consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries, continue to engage in-depth communication on the boundary question and jointly safeguard peace and tranquillity in the border areas,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told reporters. The two Asian giants share a 3,500km border, and have in the past accused each other of trying to seize territory. India’s main opposition party earlier in August that it was “deeply alarmed” by India media reports that Indian and Chinese army patrols came face-to-face in late July in the north-eastern state of Arunachal Pradesh. India’s government rejected those reports.

stories.title: Strategic talks in Paris show France and Saudi Arabia 'need each other too much'
stories.summary: The Saudi crown prince and French President Emmanuel Macron are to chair on August 24 the first meeting of the Saudi-French strategic partnership council, and a number of agreements arer expected to be signed. Among them are a new Dragon-Ball themed amusement park deal in the Paris region and the sale of French military equipment to the kingdom. FRANCE 24's Philip Turle tells us more on what to know about the talks.
